summary: RamaLama is an open-source tool that runs and serves AI models in OCI containers (Podman or Docker), pulling them from transports selected by prefix (ollama://, huggingface://, oci://, modelscope://, rlcr://, URLs). Through v0.20.0 an unprefixed model name used the Ollama transport; v0.21.0 (2026-05-14) began deprecating it, v0.23.0 (2026-06-24) relaxed that, and the code at v0.25.0 has no implicit default (names with a slash go to Hugging Face, unknown shortnames raise an error), although the README still says org-less names default to Ollama. Containers are rootless and locked down by default. Sources span GitHub (README, releases, pull requests, source), man pages, Red Hat, a blog and a forum thread.

facts.text: RamaLama makes AI models execution simple, reproducible, and container-native. It allows us to use various model registries, such as Ollama and HuggingFace, as well as ready-made images from various OCI registries. It also provides an easy path to run AI models on Podman, Docker, and even Kubernetes. Thanks to RamaLama, I was able to leverage Apple Silicon GPUs when running AI models in containers.

RamaLama is an open-source developer tool that simplifies the local serving of AI models from any source and facilitates their use for inference in production, all through the familiar language of containers.

RamaLama is an open-source tool that simplifies the local use and serving of AI models for inference from any source through the familiar approach of containers. It allows engineers to use container-centric development patterns and benefits to extend to AI use cases.
The goal of RamaLama is to make AI boring.

Distributions ship the `/usr/share/ramalama/ramalama.conf` file with their default settings. Administrators can override fields in this file by creating the `/etc/ramalama/ramalama.conf` file. Users can further modify defaults by creating the `$HOME/.config/ramalama/ramalama.conf` file. RamaLama merges its built-in defaults with specified fields from these files if they exist. Fields specified in the user's file override the administrator's file, which overrides the distribution's file, which overrides the built-in defaults.

Hosted API transports connect directly to the remote provider and bypass the local container runtime.
